methods.title: Choose the representation that owns each behavior
requires: A brief naming visual, physical, animation and lighting behavior
procedure: Classify independently moving matter as cells, shape-preserving parts as attachments, pose-dependent topology as frames, and surface response as channels.
Record multiple owners when one asset spans systems and name the conversion boundary.
checks: Every requested behavior has an owner and an explicit input/output contract.
A decorative effect does not acquire physical simulation merely because it looks granular.
pitfalls: This classification recommends an architecture; it does not make PixelLab or a renderer implement it.
A single asset may require several representations.

procedure: Classify a sand pile, hinged cannon, blinking eye, breathing highlight, normal map and wall shadow.
Expect cell, attachment, frame, cluster, surface-channel and occlusion owners respectively.
acceptance: All six owners match.
The shadow cannot be satisfied by the normal map alone.

methods.title: Declare and validate a scoped palette
requires: An approved RGBA palette, color-space choice and transparency policy
procedure: Assign stable palette indices and reserve any transparent entry explicitly.
Validate opaque pixels against the palette; keep lighting-output exemptions separately declared.
Apply color replacements by semantic ramp rather than unrestricted RGB interpolation.
checks: Every checked pixel maps to an allowed index.
Palette changes retain stable semantic meaning and transparency.
pitfalls: A fixed small palette is optional art direction, not a universal definition of pixel art.
RGBA data can be palette-constrained without using an indexed file format.

procedure: Use a 4x4 opaque image whose entries cycle through #101820, #406050, #90B070, #E0D890.
Replace one pixel with #406051 and run membership validation.
acceptance: Original has zero palette violations.
Mutant reports exactly one violating coordinate.

methods.title: Track raster connectivity and semantic clusters separately
requires: A declared 4- or 8-neighbor rule and semantic masks
procedure: Extract same-color connected components with the selected rule.
Label intentional details such as eyes, sparks and stars; these may be legal singletons.
Use semantic masks across multiple colors when a feature must be edited as a unit.
checks: Connected-component counts are reproducible.
Protected feature masks remain present after operations.
pitfalls: A semantic cluster need not be a single-color connected component.
Automatically deleting every singleton destroys legitimate detail.

procedure: Create an 8x8 image with a 2x2 body, two diagonal pixels and one isolated protected eye.
Run 4- and 8-neighbor component extraction; then delete the protected eye in a mutant.
acceptance: The diagonal pair is separate under 4-connectivity and joined under 8-connectivity.
Only the mutant fails feature preservation.

methods.title: Evaluate identity using silhouette and target backgrounds
requires: Intended viewing scale, representative backgrounds and identity landmarks

Applicability judgment: the cited cluster constraints, temporal-change discussion and UI brief support feature preservation and contextual clarity; they do not prescribe the flat-mask or multi-background procedure below.
procedure: Treat this inspection sequence as a curated expert diagnostic proposal. Select the views that answer the current asset question; do not attribute the sequence itself to the cited passages or make it an owner requirement.
Render a flat opaque mask before detailing.
Inspect major proportions, negative spaces and landmark separation at native logical scale.
Compare the colored asset on representative light, dark and busy backgrounds.
checks: Named identity landmarks remain visible at the target size.
Required gaps stay open and interactive forms separate from their surroundings.
pitfalls: Silhouette alone cannot validate faces, materials or fine symbols.
No contrast ratio or component count proves aesthetic quality.

The cited temporal silhouette-change condition is animation-specific; it does not impose a static-icon construction rule. The key fixture proves its landmark checks only, not universal aesthetic validity.

procedure: Draw a 16x16 key with a ring hole, shaft and two teeth; render mask and colored views on three backgrounds.
Create a negative example by filling the hole and merging the teeth.
acceptance: Record native-scale contact sheets and explicit pass/fail for hole, shaft and both teeth.
Negative example fails the landmark checklist; aesthetic review remains separate.

methods.title: Audit stair-step runs without imposing one contour style
requires: A contour mask and declared intentional corners or irregular regions
procedure: Trace boundary runs and highlight sudden run-length changes.
Regularize only contours intended to read as smooth.
Preserve corners, damage and organic asymmetry identified in the brief.
checks: A supplied straight diagonal retains its declared repeating step pattern.
No protected corner changes during cleanup.
pitfalls: Not every uneven run is a jaggy; shape can require an abrupt change.
Mechanical contour smoothing can erase style and identity.

procedure: Use an 8x8 45-degree one-pixel staircase and record its unit step sequence.
Add a one-cell horizontal detour at the midpoint; mark it first accidental, then intentional.
acceptance: Detour is reported in both cases with its location.
Only the accidental case is eligible for correction.

methods.title: Use material-specific value and hue ramps
requires: Named material regions and approved ordered color ramps
procedure: Build dark-to-light ramps appropriate to the material and mood.
Assign each material's pixels to its ramp and retain semantic indices.
Use hue shifts only where the art direction calls for them; inspect neighboring materials together.
checks: Ramp lookup never escapes its assigned palette.
A recolor preserves the declared ordering and region membership.
pitfalls: Hue shifting and monotonically increasing numerical luminance are choices, not universal requirements.
Different materials may intentionally share colors or intersect ramps.

procedure: Assign three ordered slots to a 3x3 metal sample.
Remap those slots to a three-color warm metal ramp without changing indices or alpha.
acceptance: All nine index assignments and alpha values are unchanged.
Only the three designated output colors occur.

methods.title: Apply authored edge antialiasing only to selected edges
requires: Approved edge ramp, edge mask and representative background
procedure: Choose intermediate colors from the approved ramp inside the selected boundary region.
Preserve required hard edges and avoid universal outlines of intermediate color.
Preview against each allowed background before accepting.
checks: Changed pixels stay within the selected edge mask and palette.
Protected hard edges remain byte-identical.
pitfalls: Background-specific intermediate colors can form halos on different backgrounds.
This is authored color placement, not a permission to enable bilinear texture filtering.

procedure: Render a 5x5 diagonal using dark, mid and bright colors with an explicit two-pixel AA mask.
Apply AA, then repeat with a forbidden interior pixel included by a buggy implementation.
acceptance: Valid output changes only the two selected pixels.
The mutant reports the out-of-mask change.

methods.title: Count dither coverage and constrain its region
requires: A tileable threshold matrix, two approved colors and a region mask
procedure: For fraction q, select cells with rank < 16*q when 16*q is integral.
Keep the pattern phase consistent across adjacent regions unless a discontinuity is intentional.
checks: Coverage is the actual selected-cell count divided by total cells.
The pattern changes only within its semantic mask.
pitfalls: The local source's example percentage labels are incorrect; count cells instead.
Dither can add noise and is optional; flat clusters may suit an asset better.

procedure: Threshold the specified 4x4 matrix at 4, 8 and 12.
Tile each result 3x3 and inspect coverage and boundary continuation.
acceptance: Selected populations are exactly 4, 8 and 12 of 16.
Each 12x12 result retains 25%, 50% or 75% coverage.

methods.title: Test repeating texture in a neighborhood
requires: Tile dimensions and a declared edge-compatibility contract
procedure: Design features that continue across wrapped boundaries.
Render a 3x3 repetition and mark dominant repeated landmarks.
For exact-match edge contracts compare opposite edge samples; for transition art inspect the declared continuation relation.
checks: The declared edge relation holds.
A native-scale neighborhood review checks visible seams and repetition.
pitfalls: Matching edge bytes is neither necessary nor sufficient for every seamless texture.
Random interior noise does not automatically hide repetition.

procedure: Build an 8x8 tile with identical opposite borders and a central 2x2 mark.
Repeat it 3x3; mutate one right-edge pixel.
acceptance: Original passes exact-border checks.
Mutant identifies the right/left mismatch; visual review still assesses repeated motifs.

methods.title: Choose and exhaustively exercise tile connectivity
requires: Named terrain labels and explicit edge, corner or mixed topology
procedure: Define the bit ordering and which neighbor relations a tile represents.
Enumerate the supported patterns and any intentional omissions.
Verify selected tiles satisfy the neighborhood labels instead of guessing topology from an image.
checks: Every declared pattern resolves or produces an explicit missing-pattern result.
Adjacent edge or corner labels agree according to the selected topology.
pitfalls: A 16-tile edge set, 16-tile corner set and 47-tile blob set encode different contracts.
Do not assume every tile generator emits the same ordering.

procedure: For binary edge labels use N=1,E=2,S=4,W=8 and generate all masks 0..15.
Join mask 2 to mask 8 horizontally and mask 4 to mask 1 vertically; also test incompatible pairs.
acceptance: All 16 masks exist exactly once.
Both valid joins pass and both mismatched-label joins fail.

methods.title: Vary interiors while preserving connectivity and lighting
requires: A base topology, allowed transformations and seeded selection policy
procedure: Group variants by identical connection labels.
Change interior details while keeping necessary boundary features compatible.
Permit flips or rotations only when directional lighting and world meaning remain valid.
checks: Variant selection never changes the required connection class.
Same seed and inputs select the same sequence when deterministic generation is requested.
pitfalls: Mirroring a shaded wall can reverse its light direction.
Variant weights describe selection policy, not a guarantee of visual variety in a small map.

procedure: Make three 8x8 tiles sharing the same border and distinct 2x2 interior marks.
Select 64 placements using a fixed documented PRNG seed; include one mutant with a changed border.
acceptance: Repeated runs produce identical variant IDs.
All originals preserve edge compatibility; the mutant fails.

methods.title: Make sheet layout and frame identity explicit
requires: Image dimensions, frame rectangles, offset, spacing, margin and ordering
procedure: Store frame rectangles and stable IDs with the sheet.
Validate in-bounds rectangles, intended overlaps, frame order and trim metadata.
Extract frames and reconstruct the logical originals before using a sheet in runtime.
checks: Each referenced frame is present and addressable.
Round-trip extraction preserves expected pixels and anchors.
pitfalls: A PNG sheet alone does not communicate playback duration, pivots or tags.
Packed atlas order can differ from semantic animation order.

procedure: Pack four distinct 3x3 frames into a 2x2 sheet with margin 1 and spacing 1; total dimensions are 9x9.
Extract at (1,1),(5,1),(1,5),(5,5); test a wrong spacing of 0.
acceptance: All four correct extractions match their source pixel arrays exactly.
Wrong-spacing extraction fails the expected image comparison.

methods.title: Carry source and adaptation intent into reusable assets
requires: Original source path, creator information if supplied, intended use and adaptation scope
procedure: Preserve the original material and record the exact excerpt used as reference.
Separate original creative examples from third-party imagery, fonts and code.
Record reuse permission evidence when distributing sourced material; if it is absent, author an original asset from the functional brief.
checks: Every reused external component has its source and reuse basis recorded.
Adaptations identify which parts were reused, redrawn or excluded.
pitfalls: An inspiration URL or a copied snippet is not a license statement.
Legacy Waylight colors and UI mandates are project-specific, not universal art rules.

procedure: Create a manifest for an original 8x8 folder icon and a second entry citing the archive's Dusan Cezek attribution.
Mark the second entry's reuse basis unresolved; attempt release-manifest validation.
acceptance: The original asset is eligible under its declared original authorship.
The sourced unresolved entry is identified before redistribution; no external code is executed.

methods.title: Trim transparent padding while preserving logical anchors
requires: Original canvas, alpha policy and an anchor in original logical coordinates
procedure: Find the permitted opaque bounds and record trim offset and original size.
Translate pivot and socket coordinates by the crop origin.
Keep restoration metadata so each frame can be reconstructed on its original canvas.
checks: Restored pixels and anchors match the untrimmed source.
No intentionally translucent edge is discarded without an explicit threshold policy.
pitfalls: A tighter image rectangle can move the sprite if its trim offset is lost.
Removing a background requires an actual mask decision, not blindly treating one RGB color as transparent.

procedure: On a transparent 16x16 canvas place a 4x5 block at (6,7) and anchor (8,11).
Crop to origin (6,7), store new anchor (2,4), then reconstruct.
acceptance: Crop is 4x5, trim offset is (6,7), local anchor is (2,4).
Reconstructed 16x16 pixels and anchor exactly match the original.

methods.title: Render at a declared logical grid and inspect device pixels
requires: Logical resolution, camera convention and target viewport dimensions
procedure: Render or sample at the logical grid, then use a declared integer scale where required.
Apply nearest sampling to image scaling and account for browser device pixel ratio.
Inspect the final output, not only a CSS property or import setting.
checks: A logical pixel expands into a uniform scale-by-scale block in the fixture.
No new colors appear during opaque nearest-neighbor enlargement.
pitfalls: Nearest filtering alone does not constrain lighting resolution.
Noninteger scaling, arbitrary rotation and browser zoom can change displayed pixel widths.

procedure: Scale a 2x2 image of four opaque distinct colors by 3 to 6x6.
Inspect every 3x3 quadrant and compare palette membership.
acceptance: Each quadrant is exactly uniform and matches its source pixel.
The final image contains exactly four colors.

methods.title: Declare alpha and compositing behavior
requires: RGBA interpretation, straight or premultiplied alpha, and allowed alpha levels
procedure: Keep alpha policy separate from RGB palette membership.
Use the chosen compositing equation consistently through export, import and display.
Inspect edges against light and dark backgrounds after round-trip import.
checks: Binary-alpha assets contain only 0 and 255 unless an exception is declared.
Composited fixtures agree with the declared alpha model.
pitfalls: Fully transparent RGB channels can differ without changing visible appearance.
Multiplying premultiplied RGB by alpha again darkens edges.

procedure: For straight alpha composite red (255,0,0,0.5) over blue (0,0,255) in a declared linear numeric fixture.
Separately validate binary-alpha pixels [0,255,127].
acceptance: Unrounded linear result is (127.5,0,127.5).
Binary-alpha validation reports only the 127 entry; display color-space conversion is a separate step.

methods.title: Author duration and event semantics per frame
requires: Ordered frame IDs, positive durations and loop or one-shot policy
procedure: Store durations explicitly rather than assuming uniform FPS.
Name anticipation, action, impact and settle events where relevant.
Define half-open time intervals so event and frame boundaries have no ambiguity.
checks: Every duration is positive and playback reaches the expected frame at boundary times.
One-shot terminal states and looping wrap behavior are explicit.
pitfalls: More frames do not automatically improve weight or readability.
Unspecified preview FPS must not overwrite authored durations.

procedure: Use frames A,B,C with durations 80,40,120 milliseconds and a looping total of 240.
Sample t=0,79,80,119,120,239,240 using half-open intervals.
acceptance: Frame IDs are A,A,B,B,C,C,A.
An impact event at 120 fires once per loop crossing.

methods.title: Track contacts and review loop closure
requires: Named anchors, ground line and expected contact intervals
procedure: Track contact-point coordinates independently from each frame's crop rectangle.
Use onion-skin or difference views to compare adjacent poses and last-to-first transition.
Permit displacement where the action demands it; lock only specified contacts.
checks: Required planted contacts remain fixed through their contact interval.
The loop boundary obeys the same motion policy as internal transitions.
pitfalls: A moving root can coexist with a visually planted foot only after world-space compensation.
A low pixel-difference score does not prove a convincing animation.

procedure: Create three 16x16 frames with a foot anchor at (8,14), varying only a body highlight.
Mutate the final frame's anchor to (9,14) and inspect last-to-first displacement.
acceptance: Original has zero foot displacement on every transition.
Mutant reports a one-pixel contact jump.

methods.title: Encode fractional edge motion with approved colors
requires: Known background, edge ramp and an edge feature mask
procedure: Construct coverage changes for the selected edge while keeping output on integer cells.
Map coverage to approved ramp entries.
Measure a luminance- or coverage-weighted centroid and inspect the motion at authored durations.
checks: Intermediate frames stay in the palette and feature region.
The chosen motion metric moves in the intended direction.
pitfalls: Apparent motion depends on contrast and viewing conditions.
This method does not place a physical sprite at a fractional logical coordinate.

procedure: Map 0,0.25,0.5,0.75,1 to five approved grayscale ramp entries.
acceptance: Total coverage is 1 in each frame.
Coverage centroids are 0,0.25,0.5,0.75,1; palette membership holds.

methods.title: Move a feature using a deliberate cluster handoff
requires: Feature mask, permitted temporary area change and connectivity rule
procedure: Establish the leading pixels before withdrawing the trailing pixels.
For narrow features use approved shade transitions if area growth is unacceptable.
Protect surrounding silhouette and feature identity.
checks: The feature remains connected under the declared rule.
Its centroid moves toward the target and any area change stays inside the declared budget.
pitfalls: Temporary widening changes volume and may be wrong for rigid material.
A mechanically valid handoff still needs visual timing review.

procedure: Use one-row masks .##.., .###., ..##. with x starting at zero.
Count cells and compute unweighted centroids.
acceptance: Areas are 2,3,2; centroids are 1.5,2,2.5.
Each feature is connected and moves right without disappearing.

methods.title: Animate internal shading while protecting silhouette
requires: Opaque mask, semantic highlight or shadow mask and approved ramps
procedure: Keep the outer occupancy stable for a subtle idle when the brief requires it.
Shift only selected internal highlights or shadows.
Review whether shading motion communicates form or incorrectly looks like moving illumination.
checks: Protected silhouette and identity pixels remain unchanged.
All changed pixels belong to the declared shading region.
pitfalls: Highlight movement may imply changing light rather than body motion.
Silhouette preservation is a local idle constraint, not a general animation rule.

procedure: Fill an 8x8 body mask at x=1..6,y=1..6 and add a two-pixel highlight at (2,3),(3,3).
Move the highlight to (3,3),(4,3) while restoring base color behind it.
acceptance: Opaque masks are identical and exactly two color samples change.
Highlight area remains 2 and its centroid moves right by 1.

methods.title: Animate dither phase with an explicit period
requires: A fixed threshold matrix, motion direction, region and positive period
procedure: Shift the pattern phase deterministically with wrapped coordinates.
Hold coverage constant when changing phase alone.
Keep stable regions untouched and preview the result at its intended scale and rate.
checks: Every phase preserves the specified population.
After one period the original pattern returns exactly.
pitfalls: Unseeded per-frame noise causes temporal boil.
Constant coverage and perfect looping do not prove that flicker is comfortable or artistically useful.

procedure: Take the 4x4 50% threshold mask from dither-coverage.
Shift x phase by 0,1,2,3,4 using modulo 4.
acceptance: Every frame has exactly 8 selected samples.
Phase 4 exactly equals phase 0; no outside-region pixel changes.

methods.title: Generate constrained supersampled in-between candidates
requires: Integer scale factor, source occupancy, approved coverage ramp and cleanup policy
procedure: Replicate occupancy to a 4x or 8x coverage grid.
Apply integer shifts in that grid, average coverage back to logical cells, and quantize to an approved ramp.
Run feature, palette and silhouette checks before any artistic acceptance.
checks: Zero shift reconstructs the source occupancy.
Translation preserves total coverage before clipping and output dimensions remain logical size.
pitfalls: Supersampling produces candidates; it is not proof of a hand-authored look.
Clipping at canvas bounds must be explicit; ramp quantization can change apparent volume.

procedure: Use a single filled cell inside an otherwise empty 5x5 image; replicate at scale 4.
Shift the high-resolution mask right by 1 sample and average 4x4 blocks.
acceptance: Coverage splits into 0.75 and 0.25 in adjacent logical cells.
Total coverage is 1 and no nonapproved ramp color appears after mapping.

methods.title: Separate rigid parts from topology-changing attachments
requires: A part hierarchy, visible attachment states and intended deformation policy
procedure: Identify regions whose pixels remain unchanged during motion.
Represent those as rigid attachments; redraw joints, faces or openings whose topology changes.
Keep bone hierarchy and visible attachment selection distinct.
checks: Every transformed part has a defined parent and pivot.
Topology-changing poses select explicit artwork rather than relying on accidental resampling.
pitfalls: Weighted mesh deformation may be valid for a chosen style but does not preserve authored clusters automatically.
The local Metal Slug-specific rig claim is unverified.

procedure: Create a 16x8 chassis, 8x4 turret and two distinct 4x4 jaw states.
Compose a four-pose sequence by translating the turret and swapping jaw state.
acceptance: Chassis and turret source pixels stay byte-identical across poses.
Jaw changes only by the selected attachment ID.

methods.title: Define pivot and socket coordinates in logical pixels
requires: Coordinate origin, pixel-center or pixel-corner convention, parent sockets and child pivots
procedure: Store socket and pivot values in the same explicit coordinate convention.
Position the child so its transformed pivot equals the parent's transformed socket.
Recalculate attachment pivots when trim offsets change.
checks: Every valid swap preserves the socket world position within the declared tolerance.
Unknown sockets or incompatible part tags fail explicitly.
pitfalls: Integer-valued pivots are not universally correct; even-size centers may be half-integer under a pixel-center convention.
Mirroring may require semantic left/right socket remapping.

procedure: Use parent socket (12,7). Attachment A has local pivot (2,3), B has pivot (5,1).
With no rotation, place A at (10,4) and B at (7,6).
acceptance: Both transformed pivots equal (12,7).
A mutant B translation of (8,6) reports a one-pixel mismatch.

methods.title: Keep continuous motion and quantize its final placement
requires: Floating-point state, logical scale, camera transform and rounding tie policy
procedure: Evaluate continuous parent and child transforms first.
Apply camera transformation before the declared screen-grid quantization boundary.
Retain unsnapped state for subsequent updates.
checks: Rendering does not overwrite simulation or animation state.
Final positions align to the declared grid with bounded rounding error.
pitfalls: Snapping every bone independently can open seams.
Tie rounding differs across languages; specify it for deterministic fixtures.

procedure: Advance x by 0.25 for eight updates from 0; use round-half-up via floor(x+0.5) for nonnegative positions.
Record continuous x and independently snapped render x.
acceptance: Continuous positions are 0.25,0.5,0.75,1,1.25,1.5,1.75,2.
Rendered positions are 0,1,1,1,1,2,2,2 and continuous state ends at 2.

methods.title: Choose a rotation strategy for each part
requires: Permitted angles, silhouette tolerance and target logical grid
procedure: Choose continuous nearest sampling, quantized angles, hand-drawn directions or an intermediate render target.
Document which visual changes are acceptable.
Evaluate extreme and intermediate poses around the actual pivot.
checks: All rendered angles follow the chosen strategy.
Every required orientation is covered, and pixel crawl is reviewed where allowed.
pitfalls: Nearest sampling and a snapped pivot do not make arbitrary rotation lossless.
A 90-degree rotation can preserve texels while changing directional lighting meaning.

procedure: Use an asymmetric 3x3 binary L mask and rotate clockwise by exact quarter-turn coordinate mapping.
Apply four quarter turns; separately inspect a 45-degree candidate.
acceptance: Four quarter turns reconstruct the original array exactly.
The 45-degree result is treated as a new raster requiring review.

methods.title: Compose independent motion channels with defined ownership
requires: Channel priorities, affected properties and event inputs
procedure: Assign locomotion, aim, recoil, damage and secondary motion to named channels.
Define override or additive behavior when channels affect the same property.
Keep attachment swaps independent of unrelated loop phase unless the action requires a reset.
checks: Every animated property has an unambiguous composition rule.
Changing one channel does not reset unrelated state.
pitfalls: Independent clips still require coordination for contacts and overlaps.
Conflicting channel writes create order-dependent results unless resolved explicitly.

procedure: Run a four-state tread loop and apply a recoil x offset [0,-2,-1,0] at tick 3.
Toggle an armor attachment at tick 5 while the tread loop continues.
acceptance: Tread indices remain 0,1,2,3 repeating without resets.
Only recoil translation and armor attachment change from the baseline.

methods.title: Atlas compatible parts and measure actual render cost
requires: Texture formats, atlas bounds, material groups and measured target renderer
procedure: Deduplicate identical raster states using content identity.
Pack compatible parts with deliberate padding and matching companion channels.
Measure memory, draw calls, texture switches and transform costs on the target integration.
checks: Source rectangles reconstruct original parts.
Performance claims include measured conditions and the relevant format or compression settings.
pitfalls: An atlas does not guarantee one draw call; blending, ordering, shaders and renderer limits can split batches.
Uncompressed byte arithmetic is an estimate, not resident memory measurement.

procedure: Compare sixty uncompressed 500x500 RGBA8 frames with twenty 64x64 parts each having eight states.
State that padding, compression, mipmaps and metadata are excluded.
acceptance: Raw estimates are 60000000 bytes and 2621440 bytes.
The result is labeled arithmetic only; runtime batching requires a separate measured scene.

methods.title: Validate normal encoding and coordinate orientation
requires: Normal axis convention, color-space interpretation and unit-vector decoder
procedure: Treat normal channels as direction data under the importer convention.
Decode and normalize with a defined fallback for degenerate vectors.
Use a directional fixture to validate handedness and green-channel orientation.
checks: Decoded vectors are finite and unit length within tolerance.
A right-facing slope responds more strongly to right-side than left-side light.
pitfalls: Applying an sRGB transfer curve to normal data changes directions.
An 8-bit flat normal is approximate; compare with quantization-aware tolerance.

procedure: Use exact float normals Nflat=(0,0,1), Nright=normalize(1,0,1), Nup=normalize(0,1,1).
Evaluate max(0,N dot L) for matching and opposite slope lights; round-trip encode C=(N+1)/2.
acceptance: Matching slope/light response equals 1; opposing slope response equals 0 within floating tolerance.
Float encoding round-trips each vector; an 8-bit implementation reports its actual angular error.

methods.title: Keep all sampled asset channels aligned
requires: Shared canvas, frame IDs, trim offsets, pivots and atlas rectangles
procedure: Apply the same crop, packing and frame ordering to corresponding channels.
Represent missing optional channels explicitly.
Use recognizable calibration marks to check sample correspondence after import.
checks: Dimensions, original sizes, trim offsets, pivots and frame IDs agree where shared UVs require it.
A channel sampled at a diffuse feature corresponds to that same feature.
pitfalls: Equal dimensions alone do not prove alignment.
Independently packed textures can be valid only when the renderer has an explicit mapping between them.

procedure: Create paired 8x8 diffuse and normal arrays with a calibration feature at (2,5).
Shift the normal feature to (3,5) while keeping dimensions identical.
acceptance: Metadata checks pass dimensions in both cases.
Pixel correspondence detects the shifted mutant; matching dimensions are not reported as sufficient proof.

methods.title: Quantize light response and optionally select palette ramps
requires: Finite intensity, K>=2 bands, clamping policy and optional material ramps
procedure: Compute or accept continuous light intensity separately from raster color.
Clamp intensity to the declared range before quantization.
For strict palette output choose a material ramp entry; multiplying RGB by a band does not itself preserve palette membership.
checks: Band index remains in 0..K-1 for finite inputs.
Ramp-output mode emits only declared colors.
pitfalls: Banding can shimmer as a light moves; inspect temporal transitions.
Lighting quantization is an optional style decision.

procedure: For K=4 use b=floor(clamp(I,0,1)*3+0.5).
Evaluate I=-1,0,0.2,0.5,0.8,1,2 and select four distinct ramp entries.
acceptance: Band indices are 0,0,1,2,2,3,3.
Every output equals one of the four entries; NaN is rejected rather than converted silently.

methods.title: Declare how dynamic light combines with baked shading
requires: Authored-shade, flat-albedo or hybrid mode and a bounded modulation strength
procedure: Record whether volume already exists in the diffuse image.
Choose dynamic-light modulation appropriate to that mode.
Compare baseline, neutral-light and opposing-light states to detect double shading.
checks: Zero modulation reproduces diffuse input.
Any palette or value clamps are explicit and applied after modulation.
pitfalls: A generated normal map can interpret painted shadows as geometry.
Strong dynamic lighting can contradict highlights already painted into the sprite.

procedure: Use scalar diffuse values [0.2,0.5,0.8] and modulation D*(1+k*(L-0.5)).
Test k=0 at L=0,0.5,1; then inspect k=0.2 on the same strip.
acceptance: All k=0 outputs exactly equal diffuse values.
The k=0.2 outputs are finite and bounded by 0.9D and 1.1D before any explicit clamping.

methods.title: Separate surface response from occlusion
requires: An explicit caster polygon, occupancy field, depth or other visibility representation
procedure: Evaluate orientation and visibility as separate terms.
Require an actual visibility representation when the asset declares shadow casting.
Choose caster simplification and light-resolution policy appropriate to the game.
checks: A normal-only asset cannot satisfy a shadow-casting contract.
Removing the occluder changes visibility while leaving surface normal response unchanged.
pitfalls: A dark diffuse patch is not evidence of a dynamic cast shadow.
Normal maps do not encode which other object blocks the light.

procedure: Use light (0,0), receiver (4,0), and an opaque vertical segment from (2,-1) to (2,1).
Trace the light-to-receiver segment with and without the occluder; keep the receiver normal fixed.
acceptance: Visibility is 0 with the intersection and 1 without it.
The fixed normal term is identical in both cases.

methods.title: Add height, masks and emission only with defined consumers
requires: Per-channel meaning, numeric range, coordinate convention and renderer consumer
procedure: Keep color, direction, height, response mask and emission distinct.
Declare packing and whether values are color data or linear data.
Reject unsupported channels at integration rather than silently treating them as active features.
checks: Every declared channel has a named consumer and documented fallback.
Response-mask zero suppresses the masked term; emission follows its own policy.
pitfalls: Extra channels increase authoring, memory and synchronization work.
An image generator returning a map does not establish that an engine consumes it correctly.

procedure: Use C=D*(A+M*L)+E with scalar D=0.5,A=0.2,L=0.8,E=0.1.
Evaluate masks M=0 and M=1, then disable emission.
acceptance: Outputs are 0.2 and 0.6 with emission, 0.1 and 0.5 without.
Channel declarations remain separate from this illustrative shader's availability.

methods.title: Use shared material definitions with per-cell mutable state
requires: Material IDs, behavior table and declared mutable state
procedure: Put immutable density or phase thresholds in material definitions.
Store occupancy, temperature, lifetime and ownership only where the simulation needs them.
Derive appearance from material and state without conflating render colors with material identity.
checks: Every nonempty cell resolves to a known material.
Palette changes cannot change physics merely by changing visible RGB.
pitfalls: The shared-table layout is a proposed architecture, not a confirmed Noita memory layout.
Decorative dust may need only a visual effect.

procedure: Create material IDs 0=empty,1=sand,2=water and a 4x4 cell array.
Change sand's display color without changing the ID grid; introduce an unknown ID in a mutant.
acceptance: The original material and physics state remain identical after recoloring.
The unknown material ID is rejected with its cell coordinate.

methods.title: Bound movement and prevent duplicate updates
requires: Tick identifiers, movement bounds, seeded tie-breaking and conflict resolution
procedure: Process gravity rules in a declared scan order.
Carry update identity with moving material so it cannot move twice unintentionally in one tick.
Resolve target conflicts deterministically and record boundary behavior.
checks: Material count is conserved for nonreactive closed-world movement.
No material entity exceeds its per-tick displacement bound; repeated runs with the same seed match.
pitfalls: Bottom-up order alone does not prevent all cross-chunk double updates.
Deterministic ties do not make different algorithms or update orders equivalent.

procedure: Use an 8x8 world with a solid floor at y=7 and sand at (3,1),(3,2),(4,1).
Permit one-cell downward or diagonal movement per tick, assign stable particle IDs, and simulate 20 ticks twice from identical state and seed.
acceptance: All three sand IDs remain present after every tick.
No ID moves more than one permitted step per tick and both final states match.

methods.title: Track active regions using rule influence bounds
requires: Chunk size, complete read/write radius, cross-boundary wake rules and reference full-scan mode
procedure: Dirty both source and destination neighborhoods when cells change.
Expand the dirty region by the complete next-step influence radius.
Sleep stable regions and wake neighboring chunks for boundary changes.
checks: Optimized and full-scan outputs agree for the same declared update semantics.
Boundary activity wakes every region that can be affected.
pitfalls: 64x64 is a source case-study choice, not a universal best chunk size.
Counting fewer cell visits demonstrates less scanning, not automatically faster wall-clock performance.

procedure: Split a 16x8 grid into two 8x8 chunks and place movable material at x=7 next to the boundary.
Run the same rule ordering in full-scan and dirty-region modes until stable.
acceptance: State hashes match after each tick.
An event crossing x=7 to x=8 wakes the right chunk, and stable regions eventually stop scanning.

methods.title: Schedule only disjoint writable cellular regions concurrently
requires: Exact job write domains, maximum displacement and barrier semantics
procedure: Compute each job's possible write domain, including halos and cascaded rule effects.
Group jobs only when these domains are disjoint.
Place required barriers between phases and re-evaluate ownership if movement bounds change.
checks: Every concurrent pair has empty write-domain intersection.
A serial execution of the same phase ordering agrees with its parallel implementation when deterministic mode is promised.
pitfalls: Copying four phases is unsafe when a different rule can write farther.
Rectangular halo estimates may be conservative; smaller shapes need proof, not assumption.

procedure: For 8x8 chunks at origins (0,0),(8,0),(16,0), use a one-cell halo and half-open write rectangles [-1,9)x[-1,9),[7,17)x[-1,9),[15,25)x[-1,9).
Check pairwise intersections and group only first and third together.
acceptance: Adjacent chunk pairs conflict.
First and third are disjoint and may share a phase under this fixture's bound.

methods.title: Encode material reactions as bounded data
requires: Known reactants, conditions, output materials, probability policy and conflict ordering
procedure: Separate immutable reaction definitions from live cell state.
Validate references, probability ranges, temperature conditions and available output space.
Define reaction priority and accounting rules before combining reactions.
checks: Unknown materials and invalid probabilities fail validation.
Reaction outcomes occur only when declared conditions hold.
pitfalls: Gameplay chemistry need not conserve real chemical mass, but its own accounting must be explicit.
Different reaction order can change results even with the same seed.

procedure: Define water -> steam when temperature >=100, with probability 1 and one-cell replacement.
Run isolated cells at temperatures 99,100,101; add a mutant rule with probability 1.2.
acceptance: Only 100 and 101 become steam and total cell occupancy is unchanged.
Probability 1.2 is rejected before simulation.

methods.title: Extract components and preserve occupancy at solver boundaries
requires: Connectivity convention, ownership transfer, contour policy and simplification tolerance
procedure: Identify connected occupied components after damage.
Extract boundaries with an explicit treatment of diagonal ambiguity, then simplify within gameplay tolerance.
Transfer ownership once and retain a mapping back to source cells.
checks: Component union equals the remaining occupancy with no duplicates.
Every occupied cell has exactly one owner at the conversion boundary.
pitfalls: Component extraction alone does not prove stable rigid-body behavior.
Contour simplification and rerasterization can alter collision shape; measure their error explicitly.

procedure: On a 7x3 mask fill x=0..2 and x=4..6 on every row, plus bridge cell (3,1).
Use 4-connectivity; remove the bridge and extract components.
acceptance: Before damage there is one 19-cell component; afterward there are two 9-cell components.
The two components partition exactly the 18 remaining cells; no solver performance claim is made.

methods.title: Validate dependency order across simulation, animation and rendering
requires: Stage dependency graph and ownership transfer points
procedure: Name simulation updates, structural conversion, animation evaluation, snapping, lighting and final presentation as separate stages.
Schedule according to actual dependencies and document any engine-specific feedback cycle.
Validate declared stage order and require capabilities for each requested output.
checks: No stage reads data before its producer or ownership transfer completes.
Continuous animation precedes final snapping; quantized lighting precedes final enlargement when that pipeline is selected.
pitfalls: The source sequence is a proposal; engine physics order may legitimately differ.
A metadata declaration is not evidence that any stage ran.

procedure: Create dependencies animation->snap->light->upscale and cells->components->physics.
Validate a topological ordering and a mutant ordering with upscale before light.
acceptance: A valid ordering passes all dependency edges.
The mutant reports the light->upscale violation and cannot claim completed rendering.

methods.title: Tie pixel UI animation to actual state and input
requires: Authoritative input or gameplay state and project-specific styling brief
procedure: Map idle, pressed, disabled and health states to explicit visual states.
Use timing only for the transition the real event triggered.
Retain static recognizability and adapt scale and color across the surrounding UI.
checks: The visual state corresponds to the supplied input or health state.
No decorative timer reports an event or progress that has not occurred.
pitfalls: The archive's keyboard prompt and Waylight palette rules belong to its original project.
A CSS demo with blur or continuous motion may conflict with a strict-grid asset profile.

procedure: For an original 8x8 interaction icon define idle, pressed and disabled masks.
Feed enabled/down/up/disabled/down events and record selected state.
acceptance: States are idle,pressed,idle,disabled,disabled.
Disabled input does not produce a pressed-success visual; source styling is not globally imposed.
